did_you_know.text: The first verse opens with three calls to praise: “Praise the Lord,” “Praise, servants of the Lord,” and “Praise the name of the Lord.” This repetition emphasizes the central place of praise in the psalm.
The psalm presents the blessing of the Lord’s name as continuing without end: “from this time forth and forevermore.”
Praise is portrayed as extending throughout the whole world, “from the rising of the sun to its setting”—from where the sun rises to where it sets.
The verse distinguishes between the Lord’s exaltation above all nations and his glory in the heavens: “The Lord is exalted over all nations, and his glory is above the heavens.”
The question “Who is like the Lord our God?” expresses the Lord’s uniqueness and unparalleled greatness.

Alongside his exalted status, the Lord is described as one who “humbles himself to see”—watching over and observing the heavens and the earth. Thus, the psalm presents exaltation and attentive care together.
The Lord is described as raising the poor from the dust and lifting the needy from the ash heap; these images emphasize a transition from lowliness to a position of honor.
The verse describes the poor being raised to the point of being seated “with princes,” that is, among people of status and importance.
At the end of the psalm, the Lord is described as giving the barren woman a home and making her “a joyful mother of children.” The psalm ends, as it began, with the words “Praise the Lord.”
